clue.text: Ordered fireman to preserve world heritage site

indicators.note: ordered here means put into a new order, so the letters of fireman to are rearranged

parts.note: jam is a fruit preserve

explanation.surface: A firefighter is told to look after a protected landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserve' looks like a verb but is a noun. The site is a twelfth-century tower in a remote valley of Afghanistan.
explanation.definitionFit: This tower in Afghanistan is listed by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site.

clue.text: Timid person tentatively starting to blame inferior cheese

parts.note: a timid, shy person is called a mouse

indicators.note: starting means only the opening letter of tentatively is taken

parts.note: to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: A shy person hesitantly begins to criticise some poor-quality cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' takes T from 'tentatively'. Mousetrap is British slang for cheap, poor-quality cheese, as if fit only for baiting traps.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang term for low-grade cheddar, the sort of cheese used as bait for rodents.

clue.text: Hazel's cooking won't burn

indicators.note: cooking suggests something being worked on or manipulated, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook named Hazel is confident her food won't burn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazel' looks like a woman's name but is a colour; 'cooking' rearranges WONTBURN.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazel is a light brown colour, like the shell of a hazelnut, which this colour term also describes.

clue.text: Ex-PM reading book in shower?

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a shower of rain

explanation.surface: A former prime minister reads in the bath or shower.
explanation.walkthrough: Yitzhak Rabin was Prime Minister of Israel, assassinated in 1995. 'Shower?' is a noun for rain, not a bathroom fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Yitzhak Rabin twice served as Israel's prime minister, so he is a former premier.

clue.text: TV scores for skiing moves

parts.note: tele is short for television
marks are scores, as given by judges

explanation.surface: Television judges award points for moves on the ski slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Telemark turns are a Norwegian style of ski turn, named after a region of Norway.

clue.text: Hurried up?

definitions.meaning: a ... visit is a hurried, brief one

explanation.definitionFit: A flying visit is a rushed one, and a plane aloft is in the air, high up.

clue.text: Playing Real, gets little time on the ball

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being toyed with, so they are rearranged

parts.note: T is a short abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A footballer playing for Real Madrid gets little time on the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges REAL into ALER; 'on the ball' looks like football but means attentive.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the ball is an idiom for being sharp and watchful.

clue.text: Type of clue with answer X

parts.note: the letter X is shaped like a cross

explanation.surface: A clue whose solution is the letter X.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords, clues are either across or down, so the definition points to the grid direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword clues are grouped into horizontal and vertical lists, this being the horizontal kind.

clue.text: Pretty mechanical? Just Bottom, enthralled by Puck, perhaps

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive inside, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: Puck is a sprite in A Midsummer Night's Dream, an example of a fairy

indicators.note: just the bottom of a word means only its final letter, here of mechanical

explanation.surface: Bottom, the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream, is one of the 'mechanicals', bewitched in the play by Puck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just Bottom' takes L, the last letter of 'mechanical', and 'enthralled by' puts it inside FAIRY. Bottom looks like the character but is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty in the sense of rather, quite, moderately, as in pretty good.

clue.text: Noble matter

definitions.meaning: a European nobleman equivalent to an earl

explanation.definitionFit: A European aristocrat holds this title, and a thing that is important is said to count.

clue.text: Ruddy stag party members start to arrive in Irish town

parts.note: ruddy and bally are both mild British euphemisms for bloody
a stag party is for men only

indicators.note: start to means just the first letter of arrive

explanation.surface: A rowdy bachelor party begins to turn up in a town in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ballymena is a town in County Antrim, Northern Ireland. A stag party is the British name for a bachelor party.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballymena is a town in County Antrim in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Porn content extended to go beyond agreed limit

parts.note: the content of porn is its middle pair of letters; extended means each of those cricket scorecard abbreviations is written out in full

explanation.surface: An adult film runs beyond its scheduled time.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket scoring O stands for over and R for run, so the middle of 'Porn', OR, is 'extended' to OVER + RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed a time or budget limit is to overshoot it, as a meeting or a project might.

clue.text: Beast in beret's no musical backing

indicators.note: backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A beret-wearing performer is no good at music and needs backing.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters RETSNOM sit across 'beret's no musical'; 'backing' reads them in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A monster is a fearsome creature, a beast in the sense of a frightening animal.

clue.text: Sort of fields amongst high waters by rivers

indicators.note: amongst places the rivers inside the rearranged letters
high means intoxicated, so the letters of waters by are scrambled

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river, so two rivers give two Rs

explanation.surface: Fields lying among the high waters beside some rivers, as in a flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' reads as a water level but means drunk, the anagram signal. The definition nods to the Beatles song Strawberry Fields Forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Strawberry Fields is a Liverpool place made famous by the Beatles song, so this word describes that kind of fields.

clue.text: All in? Completely!

parts.note: all, as in all or each one, means every
in is the abbreviation for an imperial unit of length, read the other way round

explanation.surface: Is everyone in? Totally, says someone answering with enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives INCH because 'in' is the standard abbreviation for that unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone entirely or thoroughly something, as in a true gentleman through and through.

clue.text: Spot? Yes, essentially a mole

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core of the word yes, its middle letter

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a mark on the skin is basically just a mole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' and 'mole' suggest skin blemishes; 'Spot' is a verb meaning to see, and the mole is an undercover agent.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to catch sight of it or notice it.

clue.text: Some of those 5 get led astray? What a pity about that

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the exclamation goes around the other piece

parts.note: shucks is an exclamation of mild disappointment

indicators.note: astray means gone off course, so the letters of led are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some of the flying ones are led off course; what a shame.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' refers to the answer to 5 down, FLYING, so the definition is birds that fly. Shucks is an American exclamation of mild regret.
explanation.definitionFit: These large ducks are birds, and so belong among things that fly.

clue.text: Pose as model in topless play

indicators.note: in puts the model's letter inside the shortened word
topless means the first letter is cut off the word for play

parts.note: play means freedom of movement or scope, as does latitude
the Model T was an early Ford car

explanation.surface: Someone poses as a model in a play without a top on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' cuts the L from LATITUDE, leaving ATITUDE, and 'in' puts T inside it. 'Pose' is the noun: a stance or ballet position.
explanation.definitionFit: In ballet, an attitude is a particular pose; generally, a pose is a bodily stance or position.

clue.text: "Father, we have sinned" — last two leaving one of the Orkney Islands

parts.note: papa is a name for one's father

indicators.note: last two leaving means the final pair of letters is dropped

parts.note: to have strayed is to have sinned, gone from the right path

explanation.surface: A confession to a priest, then two people leave one of the Scottish isles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last two leaving' drops the ED from STRAYED to leave STRAY. Orkney is an island group off northern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Papa Westray is a small island in the Orkney archipelago off northern Scotland.

clue.text: Fruit women put in babyfood as winter starts

indicators.note: put in says the women's letter goes inside the babyfood word

parts.note: pap is soft food for babies

indicators.note: starts takes the first letter of each of the words as and winter

explanation.surface: Fruit is added to babyfood as the cold season begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Pap is an old word for soft mushy food for infants; 'starts' takes the first letter of both 'as' and 'winter'.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaya, a tropical fruit, is also known by this name, as is the North American custard-apple.

clue.text: Jumbo crossword compilers? They're often 5

parts.note: a jumbo is a jumbo jet, the Boeing 747
crossword compilers are known as setters

explanation.surface: Setters of very large crosswords are often on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' means the answer to 5 down, FLYING; 'Jumbo' looks like a size but is the aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy socialites who travel the world are often in the air on planes.

clue.text: See 24 across
Be a surfer, initially wearing surprisingly sober clothes

indicators.note: clothes used as a verb means covers or wraps around
surprisingly means turned out unexpectedly, so the letters of sober are rearranged
initially takes just the first letter of wearing

explanation.surface: A surfer turns up in unexpectedly sober clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges SOBER into BROSE, which 'clothes' (a verb) wraps around W. The surfer is on the internet, not a wave.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse is to look casually through websites, which is what an internet surfer does.

clue.text: See 18
Bombardment of note across area 11 by 5

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so the note goes either side of the other pieces

parts.note: so (or soh) is a note of the sol-fa scale
eleven times five is fifty-five, written LV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A musical note stretches across a rectangle eleven by five.
explanation.walkthrough: '11 by 5' looks like dimensions but is a multiplication: 55, in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, a barrage or bombardment.

clue.text: Repair of these second houses still to be detailed in expense accounts

indicators.note: houses means contains, so one piece sits inside the other
repair of means remaking, so the letters of these are rearranged
detailed means cut off its tail, losing the last letter

parts.note: still air is windless

explanation.surface: Repairs to MPs' second homes being itemised in expense claims, echoing the 2009 British expenses scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as itemised but means losing a tail. The surface recalls British MPs claiming for repairs to second homes in 2009.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for expense claims, implying they are padded to cheat the employer.

clue.text: Some "yards per minute" swimmers

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Swimmers' speeds given in yards per minute.
explanation.walkthrough: SPERM sits across 'yards per minute'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sperm cells swim with their tails, so they can be called swimmers.

clue.text: Concession from NATO? For one, that hurt

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: NATO is a military alliance of nations
the Roman numeral for one is I
ow is a cry when something hurts

explanation.surface: A concession by NATO, which hurt one member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For one' means in place of one: the I (Roman one) in the word for NATO's kind of body is swapped for a cry of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A concession or allowance is something permitted or granted, such as a discount or a permission.

clue.text: Letter from Greece returning share in full

indicators.note: returning means the Greek letter is read backwards

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a cut is a share, as of profits

explanation.surface: A letter from Greece comes back with a full share of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns NU into UN.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncut film or text is shown complete, without anything removed.

clue.text: Play set in ultimately the worst off part of London

indicators.note: set in means the play goes inside the rearranged letters
off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately means the final letter of the word the

parts.note: Hamlet is Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A play set in the poorest part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the last letter of 'the' with 'worst'. Tower Hamlets is a deprived East London borough, which makes the surface nearly literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tower Hamlets is a borough in the East End of London.
